title: How E-Scooters Impact Shared Mobility and Consumer Safety

package_source.dataset_title: Replication Data for: How E-Scooters Impact Shared Mobility and Consumer Safety

eligible_reason: Single adoption date and excluded estimator. In data_main.csv all 265 treated census tracts switch on in the same week (yearweek 201925, Chicago's June 2019 e-scooter pilot); 470 tracts are never treated; 41 weeks (201902-201942); treatment never switches off. Every main table (Tables 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 11) is a generalized synthetic control (gsynth, interactive FE with r chosen by CV in 0-5, time-trended covariates). Table 9 is a 2x2 DiD on aggregated trip shares (lm(prop ~ close_vs_far * trip_type)). No staggered design exists, so not a near-miss.
design_notes: Census tract x week panel (735 tracts). gsynth(Y ~ treat + covariate x time_trend terms, index = c(GEOID, yearweek), force = 'two-way', EM = TRUE, CV = TRUE, r = c(0,5), bootstrap SEs). Outcomes: short rideshare trips, bikeshare trips, street and vehicle crimes; SafeGraph visits (Table 8); heterogeneity by race and age (Tables 5-6) and by day/time/crime type (Tables 10-11).
data_access: public (CC BY; Chicago open data on trips and crimes, SafeGraph visits)
main_text_note: Published article checked: e-scooters entered the Chicago pilot area on June 15, 2019 (one date); generalized synthetic control is the main estimator (Table 4 onward); synthetic DiD and alternative control groups are robustness checks reported in Web Appendix B; Table 7 is an overview of the mechanism analyses (not an estimation table); Table 9 is the 2x2 DiD on aggregated shares.
screener_notes: The rar was extracted except rideshare_binned_trip.csv (1.86 GB) and bikeshare_binned_trip.csv (1.19 GB), which feed only Figures 4-5 (trip counts by distance from e-scooter trips); they remain inside the archive. Cohort check: python3 -I cohorts.py on data_main.csv (GEOID, yearweek, treat). The Rmd has no Table 7; the article's Table 7 is an overview of mechanism analyses.
